components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
史 (history) — a hand 又 holding a record, the scribe. 史 sounds the same as 使 shǐ and 驶 shǐ.
人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 这是有史以来最热的一年。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yǒushǐyǐlái zuì rè de yì nián.
example.english: This is the hottest year since records began.
example.fact: According to NASA and NOAA climate records extending back to 1880, the ten warmest years ever recorded have all occurred since 2010, with global average temperatures now roughly 1.1-1.2°C above the pre-industrial baseline used by climate scientists.

examples.hanzi: 这是有史以来最好看的电影。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yǒushǐyǐlái zuì hǎokàn de diànyǐng.
examples.english: This is the best movie ever made.

examples.hanzi: 今年夏天有史以来最热。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián xiàtiān yǒushǐyǐlái zuì rè.
examples.english: This summer is the hottest on record.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and binding, as in 红, 给, 经: an agreement binds like a cord.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for yuē; 勺 also in 药 yào and 钓 diào.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 我们约定明天下午见面。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yuēdìng míngtiān xiàwǔ jiànmiàn.
example.english: We agreed to meet tomorrow afternoon.
example.fact: The Geneva Conventions, first adopted in 1864 and expanded after both World Wars, establish international standards for humanitarian treatment during war. Nearly every country in the world, 196 in total, is now a party to them, making them among the most universally ratified treaties in history.

examples.hanzi: 我们约定每年见一次面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yuēdìng měi nián jiàn yí cì miàn.
examples.english: We agreed to meet once a year.

examples.hanzi: 别忘了我们的约定。
examples.pinyin: Bié wàng le wǒmen de yuēdìng.
examples.english: Don't forget our agreement.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 阶, 障; 防 is a dike to guard against floods, then to defend.
方 (fāng) gives the sound: 防 fáng is close, as in 房 fáng and 妨 fáng.
止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.hanzi: 洗手可以防止细菌传播。
example.pinyin: Xǐshǒu kěyǐ fángzhǐ xìjūn chuánbò.
example.english: Washing your hands can prevent the spread of germs.
example.fact: In 1847, Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis found that hospital deaths from childbed fever dropped dramatically when doctors washed their hands with chlorinated lime before examining patients. His colleagues largely rejected the idea since germ theory wasn't yet accepted, and he died in an asylum before handwashing became standard medical practice decades later.

examples.hanzi: 戴头盔可以防止受伤。
examples.pinyin: Dài tóukuī kěyǐ fángzhǐ shòushāng.
examples.english: Wearing a helmet can prevent injuries.

examples.hanzi: 为了防止迟到，他定了两个闹钟。
examples.pinyin: Wèile fángzhǐ chídào, tā dìng le liǎng ge nàozhōng.
examples.english: To avoid being late, he set two alarms.

components.note: 亻 (person) — Buddha is a person; the same part marks people, as in 仙 immortal, 你 you.
弗 (fú) gives the sound as in 仿佛 fǎng fú; it also sounds out 费 fèi and 拂 fú.

example.hanzi: 很多人去寺庙拜佛。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén qù sìmiào bài fó.
example.english: Many people go to the temple to worship the Buddha.
example.fact: 佛 is short for 佛陀, a transliteration of "Buddha." It makes 佛教 (Buddhism), 佛像 (Buddha statue) and 佛山 (Foshan). In 仿佛 (as if) it is read fú, and the Fujian dish 佛跳墙 is named "Buddha jumps over the wall."

examples.hanzi: 他的奶奶信佛。
examples.pinyin: Tā de nǎinai xìn fó.
examples.english: His grandmother is a Buddhist.

examples.hanzi: 那座山上有一尊很大的佛像。
examples.pinyin: Nà zuò shān shàng yǒu yì zūn hěn dà de fóxiàng.
examples.english: There is a very large Buddha statue on that mountain.

components.note: 小 (small) — 小 above 大 — a small top over a big base is a point.

example.hanzi: 这支铅笔的头很尖。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiānbǐ de tóu hěn jiān.
example.english: The tip of this pencil is very sharp.
example.fact: 尖 describes points and sharp sounds: 尖叫 (to shriek), 笔尖 (pen nib). 耳朵尖 means having sharp hearing, and 尖子生 are the top students, the "tips" of the class.

examples.hanzi: 他的耳朵很尖，什么都听得到。
examples.pinyin: Tā de ěrduo hěn jiān, shénme dōu tīng de dào.
examples.english: He has sharp ears and can hear everything.

examples.hanzi: 山顶是尖的，很难爬上去。
examples.pinyin: Shāndǐng shì jiān de, hěn nán pá shàngqù.
examples.english: The mountain top is pointed and hard to climb.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 经, 系: a pulled-tight cord. The top part is also in 坚 jiān (firm).
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.

example.hanzi: 这些细节其实无关紧要。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē xìjié qíshí wúguānjǐnyào.
example.english: These details are actually insignificant.
example.fact: The 'butterfly effect,' a term coined by meteorologist Edward Lorenz in the 1960s, describes how a seemingly insignificant change — like rounding a number in a weather simulation from six decimal places to three — can lead to wildly different long-term outcomes, a discovery that helped found the field of chaos theory.

examples.hanzi: 别担心，这只是无关紧要的小事。
examples.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, zhè zhǐshì wúguānjǐnyào de xiǎoshì.
examples.english: Don't worry, it's just an insignificant little thing.

examples.hanzi: 他回答得无关紧要，大家都听不懂。
examples.pinyin: Tā huídá de wúguānjǐnyào, dàjiā dōu tīng bu dǒng.
examples.english: His answer was beside the point, and nobody could follow.

meanings: to have an instant attraction to sb
(of electricity, after an outage) to come back

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).

example.hanzi: 手机显示有一个来电。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī xiǎnshì yǒu yí gè láidiàn.
example.english: The phone shows there is an incoming call.
example.fact: The first mobile phone call was made in April 1973 by Motorola engineer Martin Cooper, who called a rival researcher at Bell Labs while standing on a New York City street with a prototype handset that weighed over a kilogram and offered just 30 minutes of talk time per charge.

examples.hanzi: 我刚才有一个来电，是妈妈打的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāngcái yǒu yí ge láidiàn, shì māma dǎ de.
examples.english: I just had an incoming call, and it was from Mom.

examples.hanzi: 你的手机来电了，快接吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī láidiàn le, kuài jiē ba.
examples.english: Your phone is ringing, pick it up.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).

example.hanzi: 他常说做坏事迟早会有报应。
example.pinyin: Tā cháng shuō zuò huàishì chízǎo huì yǒu bàoyìng.
example.english: He often says that doing bad things will eventually have consequences.
example.fact: The concept of karma originates in ancient Indian religious traditions, appearing in Hindu texts like the Upanishads composed as early as 800 BCE, where it described a cosmic law of cause and effect governing actions across multiple lifetimes — long before the word entered everyday English as shorthand for 'what goes around comes around.'

examples.hanzi: 人们常说，坏事做多了会有报应。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen cháng shuō, huàishì zuò duō le huì yǒu bàoyìng.
examples.english: People often say doing too many bad things brings retribution.

examples.hanzi: 这是他应得的报应。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā yīngdé de bàoyìng.
examples.english: This is the retribution he deserved.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.hanzi: 我们计划去海边度假。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jìhuà qù hǎibiān dùjià.
example.english: We're planning to go on vacation at the seaside.
example.fact: The Dead Sea's shoreline, about 430 meters below sea level, is the lowest point on Earth's land surface accessible on foot. Its extremely high salt concentration, nearly ten times saltier than the ocean, lets swimmers float on the surface almost without effort.

examples.hanzi: 夏天的海边人特别多。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān de hǎibiān rén tèbié duō.
examples.english: In summer the beach is especially crowded.

examples.hanzi: 我们在海边散步，看日落。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài hǎibiān sànbù, kàn rìluò.
examples.english: We took a walk by the sea and watched the sunset.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — flowers and growth: 花, 草, 茶; 荣 (from 榮) is a tree 木 in full bloom: flourishing, honor.
光 (light) — shining light; 耀 is to shine or dazzle.
翟 (dí) is a loose sound clue; it also sounds out 曜 yào and 濯 zhuó.

example.hanzi: 赢得冠军是全队的荣耀。
example.pinyin: Yíngdé guànjūn shì quán duì de róngyào.
example.english: Winning the championship is an honor for the whole team.
example.fact: Ancient Olympic champions in Greece received only an olive wreath cut from a sacred tree near the Temple of Zeus at Olympia, yet victors often received lifelong honors back home, including free meals, tax exemptions, and statues erected in their likeness — glory mattered more than material prizes.

examples.hanzi: 这座奖杯是球队的荣耀。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò jiǎngbēi shì qiúduì de róngyào.
examples.english: This trophy is the team's glory.

examples.hanzi: 能为国家工作是他的荣耀。
examples.pinyin: Néng wèi guójiā gōngzuò shì tā de róngyào.
examples.english: Working for his country is his honor.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 肚 belly, 脚 foot, 脸 face, 胖 fat; 脑 is the brain.
The right half shows hair over a skull and also sounds out 恼 nǎo and 瑙 nǎo.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.

example.hanzi: 那个画面一直浮现在我的脑海中。
example.pinyin: Nàge huàmiàn yìzhí fúxiàn zài wǒ de nǎohǎi zhōng.
example.english: That image keeps surfacing in my mind.
example.fact: The human brain generates roughly 20 watts of power, enough to dimly light a small LED bulb, yet it consumes about 20% of the body's total energy despite making up only around 2% of body weight — a reminder of how metabolically expensive thought and memory actually are.

examples.hanzi: 我的脑海里全是你的声音。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de nǎohǎi lǐ quán shì nǐ de shēngyīn.
examples.english: My mind is full of your voice.

examples.hanzi: 一个好主意突然闪过他的脑海。
examples.pinyin: Yí ge hǎo zhǔyi tūrán shǎnguò tā de nǎohǎi.
examples.english: A good idea suddenly flashed through his mind.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding the reins.
空 (kōng) is a close sound clue for kòng; 空 also in 腔 qiāng and 孔 kǒng.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 说 say, 问 ask; 告 is "to tell". 告 also gives sound to 造 zào and 靠 kào.

example.hanzi: 她向法院控告这家公司欺诈。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàng fǎyuàn kònggào zhè jiā gōngsī qīzhà.
example.english: She accused the company of fraud in court.
example.fact: The Salem witch trials of 1692-93 in colonial Massachusetts saw over 200 people accused of witchcraft based largely on testimony now understood as mass hysteria; 19 were executed before the governor intervened. Massachusetts didn't formally apologize and clear the names of all the accused until 2022, 330 years later.

examples.hanzi: 他们控告邻居制造噪音。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen kònggào línjū zhìzào zàoyīn.
examples.english: They accused their neighbor of making noise.

examples.hanzi: 被控告的人有权请律师。
examples.pinyin: Bèi kònggào de rén yǒuquán qǐng lǜshī.
examples.english: A person who is accused has the right to hire a lawyer.

components.note: 穴 (cave) — marks holes and hollows, as in 空 empty, 窗 window; 窝 is a nest or den.
呙 (guō) — loose sound hint (wō); same part in 锅 guō and 蜗 wō.

example.hanzi: 小鸟在树上做了一个窝。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo niǎo zài shù shàng zuò le yí ge wō.
example.english: The little bird built a nest in the tree.
example.fact: 窝 is a nest or den, and also the measure word for a litter or brood: 一窝小猫. 被窝 is the cozy space under the blanket, and 窝 as a verb means to stay cooped up, 窝在家里. 酒窝 is a dimple.

examples.hanzi: 小狗在沙发上窝着睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu zài shāfā shàng wō zhe shuìjiào.
examples.english: The little dog is curled up sleeping on the sofa.

examples.hanzi: 我周末不想出门，就想在家里窝着。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò bù xiǎng chūmén, jiù xiǎng zài jiālǐ wō zhe.
examples.english: I do not want to go out this weekend, just stay cozy at home.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — marks cloth and hangings, as in 布 cloth, 帜; 幢 was a curtain or banner, and is now the measure word for buildings.
童 (tóng) — loose sound hint (chuáng vs tóng); 童 also sounds out 撞 zhuàng.

example.hanzi: 那幢楼有三十层。
example.pinyin: Nà zhuàng lóu yǒu sānshí céng.
example.english: That building has thirty floors.
example.fact: As a measure word, 幢 counts buildings (一幢楼, 一幢房子), much like 栋 (dòng). Its older reading chuáng is for banners and for 幢幢, the sense of flickering shadows, as in 鬼影幢幢.

examples.hanzi: 我们住在前面那幢楼里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhù zài qiánmiàn nà zhuàng lóu lǐ.
examples.english: We live in that building in front.

examples.hanzi: 这幢房子是去年盖的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhuàng fángzi shì qùnián gài de.
examples.english: This house was built last year.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁; 镇 first meant to weigh down with metal.
真 (zhēn) — near sound — 镇 is zhèn; 真 also sounds out 慎 shèn and 填 tián.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 这个小镇子只有几百口人。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo zhènzi zhǐyǒu jǐ bǎi kǒu rén.
example.english: This small town only has a few hundred people.
example.fact: Whittier, Alaska, is a small town where nearly the entire population of around 200 people lives inside a single 14-story former U.S. Army building called Begich Towers, sharing one building for homes, the police station, a school, and a grocery store — largely due to the extreme winter isolation of the area.

examples.hanzi: 我们住在一个安静的镇子里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhù zài yí ge ānjìng de zhènzi lǐ.
examples.english: We live in a quiet town.

examples.hanzi: 镇子上只有一家小超市。
examples.pinyin: Zhènzi shàng zhǐyǒu yì jiā xiǎo chāoshì.
examples.english: There is only one small supermarket in the town.

components.note: 车 (vehicle) — wheeled transport, as in 轮 wheel, 辆 measure word for cars.
乔 (qiáo) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 桥 qiáo, 骄 jiāo and 娇 jiāo.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 他新买了一辆红色轿车。
example.pinyin: Tā xīn mǎi le yí liàng hóngsè jiàochē.
example.english: He just bought a new red sedan.
example.fact: The Ford Model T, produced from 1908 to 1927, was the first car mass-produced on a moving assembly line, cutting the time to build one chassis from over 12 hours to about 93 minutes. The resulting drop in price made car ownership possible for millions of ordinary American families for the first time.

examples.hanzi: 他开轿车去机场接朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā kāi jiàochē qù jīchǎng jiē péngyou.
examples.english: He drove his car to the airport to pick up a friend.

examples.hanzi: 这辆轿车的空间很大。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng jiàochē de kōngjiān hěn dà.
examples.english: This sedan has a lot of space.

components.note: 走 (run, walk) — movement: 起 rise, 越 cross, 赶 hurry, 趣; 超 is to jump over, surpass.
召 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 招 zhāo, 绍 shào, 照 zhào.
走 (walk, run) — movement: 起, 超, 趣, 赶; 越 is to cross over, to exceed.
戉 (yuè) sounds exactly like 越.

example.hanzi: 他的成绩超越了所有人的预期。
example.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì chāoyuè le suǒyǒu rén de yùqí.
example.english: His results surpassed everyone's expectations.
example.fact: Usain Bolt's 2009 world record of 9.58 seconds in the 100-meter sprint remains unbroken as of the mid-2020s. Biomechanical analysis showed he reached a peak speed of about 27.8 mph (44.7 km/h) partway through the race, among the fastest a human has ever been recorded running.

examples.hanzi: 这辆跑车很快就超越了前面的车。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng pǎochē hěn kuài jiù chāoyuè le qiánmiàn de chē.
examples.english: The sports car quickly overtook the cars ahead.

examples.hanzi: 他不断努力，想超越自己。
examples.pinyin: Tā búduàn nǔlì, xiǎng chāoyuè zìjǐ.
examples.english: He keeps working hard, aiming to surpass himself.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 他明明知道答案,却不说。
example.pinyin: Tā míngmíng zhīdào dá'àn, què bù shuō.
example.english: He obviously knew the answer, but didn't say it.
example.fact: The Dunning-Kruger effect, described by psychologists Justin Kruger and David Dunning in 1999, found that people with low competence in a skill often overestimate their ability more than experts do — meaning the people most obviously wrong about something are frequently the least aware of it.

examples.hanzi: 你明明答应了我，怎么又忘了？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ míngmíng dāyìng le wǒ, zěnme yòu wàng le?
examples.english: You clearly promised me, so how did you forget again?

examples.hanzi: 这明明是我的书，你怎么拿走了？
examples.pinyin: Zhè míngmíng shì wǒ de shū, nǐ zěnme názǒu le?
examples.english: This is obviously my book, so why did you take it?

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — careful words; also in 说 say, 话 speech.
堇 (jǐn) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 勤 qín.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and attitudes, as in 快 happy, 慢 slow; a careful heart.
真 (zhēn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 镇 zhèn and 填 tián.

example.hanzi: 投资的时候一定要谨慎。
example.pinyin: Tóuzī de shíhòu yídìng yào jǐnshèn.
example.english: You must be cautious when investing.
example.fact: Nuclear reactor operators follow a principle called 'defense in depth,' which stacks multiple independent, redundant safety systems so that no single failure can cause a meltdown. The approach was reinforced further after the 1979 Three Mile Island accident and again after Fukushima in 2011, each time adding new layers of caution to reactor design worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 过马路要谨慎，注意来往的车辆。
examples.pinyin: Guò mǎlù yào jǐnshèn, zhùyì láiwǎng de chēliàng.
examples.english: Be careful when crossing the road and watch for traffic.

examples.hanzi: 他做事一向很谨慎。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòshì yíxiàng hěn jǐnshèn.
examples.english: He has always been cautious in his work.

components.note: 合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and binding, as in 红, 给, 经: an agreement binds like a cord.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for yuē; 勺 also in 药 yào and 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 双方已经签订了合约。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng yǐjīng qiāndìng le héyuē.
example.english: Both parties have already signed the contract.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved into a basalt stele around 1754 BC in ancient Babylon, is one of the oldest surviving written legal codes. It included detailed rules governing contracts for trade, loans, and labor, showing that formal, enforceable agreements between parties are one of civilization's oldest legal inventions.

examples.hanzi: 这份合约有效期是两年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn héyuē yǒuxiàoqī shì liǎng nián.
examples.english: This contract is valid for two years.

examples.hanzi: 签合约之前，请仔细看清楚。
examples.pinyin: Qiān héyuē zhīqián, qǐng zǐxì kàn qīngchu.
examples.english: Please read it carefully before signing the contract.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and plants, as in 树, 林, 村; 植 is to plant.
直 (zhí) gives the sound exactly: 植 zhí, also in 值 zhí and 殖 zhí.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 阳光对植物的生长非常重要。
example.pinyin: Yángguāng duì zhíwù de shēngzhǎng fēicháng zhòngyào.
example.english: Sunlight is very important for plant growth.
example.fact: The Pando aspen colony in Utah is a single organism made up of over 40,000 genetically identical tree trunks connected by one shared root system, covering about 106 acres and estimated to be thousands of years old — one of the largest and oldest living organisms on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 这种植物不需要经常浇水。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zhíwù bù xūyào jīngcháng jiāoshuǐ.
examples.english: This kind of plant doesn't need frequent watering.

examples.hanzi: 热带雨林里有很多珍贵的植物。
examples.pinyin: Rèdài yǔlín lǐ yǒu hěn duō zhēnguì de zhíwù.
examples.english: Tropical rainforests have many precious plants.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 政府官员出席了这次会议。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ guānyuán chūxí le zhè cì huìyì.
example.english: Government officials attended this meeting.
example.fact: Imperial China's civil service examination system, which selected government officials based on merit through rigorous written tests on classical texts, ran in some form for roughly 1,300 years, from the Sui dynasty until it was abolished in 1905 — one of history's longest-running standardized meritocratic institutions.

examples.hanzi: 一位官员回答了记者的问题。
examples.pinyin: Yí wèi guānyuán huídá le jìzhě de wèntí.
examples.english: An official answered the reporters' questions.

examples.hanzi: 这位官员在会上宣布了新计划。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi guānyuán zài huì shàng xuānbù le xīn jìhuà.
examples.english: This official announced the new plan at the meeting.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — cliffs and rocks, as in 厅 hall, 厚 thick: a spring flowing from a cliff.
泉 (spring) — water from the rock: the source (源 yuán adds 氵 later); 原 is source, origin.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister.
台 (tái) is a loose sound clue for shǐ; the same 台 gives 治 zhì and 怡 yí.

example.hanzi: 考古学家发现了原始人类使用的工具。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā fāxiàn le yuánshǐ rénlèi shǐyòng de gōngjù.
example.english: Archaeologists discovered tools used by primitive humans.
example.fact: The Lomekwi 3 site in Kenya contains stone tools dated to about 3.3 million years ago, predating the genus Homo entirely — meaning some of the earliest known toolmakers may have been australopithecines, not humans, pushing back the origin of technology far earlier than scientists once assumed.

examples.hanzi: 这座森林还保持着原始的样子。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò sēnlín hái bǎochí zhe yuánshǐ de yàngzi.
examples.english: This forest still keeps its original look.

examples.hanzi: 请保存好原始数据，不要删除。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎocún hǎo yuánshǐ shùjù, bú yào shānchú.
examples.english: Please keep the original data and don't delete it.

meanings: world of a particular locale and era

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.

example.hanzi: 爱因斯坦的理论改变了我们对时空的理解。
example.pinyin: Àiyīnsītǎn de lǐlùn gǎibiàn le wǒmen duì shíkōng de lǐjiě.
example.english: Einstein's theory changed our understanding of space-time.
example.fact: Einstein's general theory of relativity, published in 1915, describes gravity not as a force but as the curvature of four-dimensional space-time caused by mass. That prediction was confirmed in 2015 when the LIGO observatory directly detected gravitational waves rippling through space-time from two colliding black holes over a billion light-years away.

examples.hanzi: 这部科幻电影讲的是穿越时空的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù kēhuàn diànyǐng jiǎng de shì chuānyuè shíkōng de gùshi.
examples.english: This sci-fi movie is about a story of traveling through time and space.

examples.hanzi: 博物馆展示了不同时空的文化。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn zhǎnshì le bùtóng shíkōng de wénhuà.
examples.english: The museum shows cultures from different times and places.

components.note: 凯 (kǎi) — triumph, mostly seen in names; as a part it sounds out 铠 kǎi and 恺 kǎi.
珏 (two jades) — the same strings shape as in 琴 qín; 瑟 is a large zither, seen in 琴瑟 and foreign names.
王 (jade, 斜玉旁) — gems and jade, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 珠 pearl; 琳 is a beautiful gem.
林 (lín) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 凯瑟琳是这所学校最优秀的学生。
example.pinyin: Kǎisèlín shì zhè suǒ xuéxiào zuì yōuxiù de xuéshēng.
example.english: Catherine is the best student at this school.
example.fact: Catherine the Great ruled the Russian Empire from 1762 to 1796, the longest reign of any female ruler in Russian history, and oversaw a massive territorial expansion that added over 200,000 square miles to the empire, including much of modern-day Ukraine and Crimea.

examples.hanzi: 凯瑟琳每天早上跑步。
examples.pinyin: Kǎisèlín měi tiān zǎoshang pǎobù.
examples.english: Catherine goes jogging every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我给凯瑟琳打了个电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi Kǎisèlín dǎ le ge diànhuà.
examples.english: I made a phone call to Catherine.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.

example.hanzi: 长期糖尿病可能引发神经病。
example.pinyin: Chángqī tángniàobìng kěnéng yǐnfā shénjīngbìng.
example.english: Long-term diabetes can lead to neuropathy.
example.fact: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy, nerve damage caused by prolonged high blood sugar, affects roughly half of all people with diabetes at some point and is one of the leading causes of numbness and pain in the feet and hands worldwide, according to the World Health Organization.

examples.hanzi: 他最近得了神经病，医生让他多休息。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn dé le shénjīngbìng, yīshēng ràng tā duō xiūxi.
examples.english: He recently developed a nerve disorder, and the doctor told him to rest more.

examples.hanzi: 这类神经病需要长期治疗。
examples.pinyin: Zhè lèi shénjīngbìng xūyào chángqī zhìliáo.
examples.english: This kind of nerve disease requires long-term treatment.

meanings: plastics (general term for synthetic polymer materials)

components.note: 土 (earth) — clay and ground; 塑 is to model in clay, as in 地 ground, 城 city.
朔 (shuò) is a loose clue; 溯 sù (to trace back) shares it and sounds the same as 塑.
斗 (dipper, measure) — measuring grain and liquids: 科, 斜, 升; 料 is rice 米 measured out, then material.

example.hanzi: 海洋里漂浮着大量塑料垃圾。
example.pinyin: Hǎiyáng lǐ piāofú zhe dàliàng sùliào lājī.
example.english: Large amounts of plastic waste float in the ocean.
example.fact: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch, a floating accumulation of plastic debris in the North Pacific Ocean, is estimated to cover an area roughly three times the size of France — though it is not a solid island but a diffuse zone where plastic concentration is far higher than in the surrounding water.

examples.hanzi: 请不要使用一次性塑料袋。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào shǐyòng yícìxìng sùliào dài.
examples.english: Please don't use disposable plastic bags.

examples.hanzi: 这个玩具是塑料做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wánjù shì sùliào zuò de.
examples.english: This toy is made of plastic.

meanings: first of the ten Heavenly Stems

components.note: 甲 (jiǎ) — shell, armour, first of the heavenly stems; as a part it sounds out 钾 jiǎ and 胛 jiǎ.

example.hanzi: 甲方和乙方要签合同。
example.pinyin: Jiǎfāng hé yǐfāng yào qiān hétong.
example.english: Party A and Party B need to sign the contract.
example.fact: 甲 is the first of the Heavenly Stems (甲乙丙丁), so it means "first" or "A": 甲方 (Party A) in contracts, and 桂林山水甲天下 (Guilin's scenery is the best under heaven). Also 指甲 (fingernail) and 甲骨文 (oracle bone script).

examples.hanzi: 甲和乙是同一个公司的同事。
examples.pinyin: Jiǎ hé yǐ shì tóng yí ge gōngsī de tóngshì.
examples.english: A and B are colleagues at the same company.

examples.hanzi: 乌龟有一层硬硬的甲。
examples.pinyin: Wūguī yǒu yì céng yìngyìng de jiǎ.
examples.english: A turtle has a hard shell.

components.note: 月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 病人每天要按时服用两次药。
example.pinyin: bìngrén měitiān yào ànshí fúyòng liǎng cì yào.
example.english: The patient must take the medicine on time twice a day.
example.fact: Penicillin, the first true antibiotic, was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 after he noticed mold accidentally contaminating a petri dish had killed the surrounding bacteria; it entered widespread medical use in the 1940s and dramatically reduced deaths from bacterial infection during World War II.

examples.hanzi: 这种药饭后服用效果最好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào fàn hòu fúyòng xiàoguǒ zuì hǎo.
examples.english: This medicine works best when taken after meals.

examples.hanzi: 孕妇不能随便服用这类药物。
examples.pinyin: Yùnfù bù néng suíbiàn fúyòng zhè lèi yàowù.
examples.english: Pregnant women shouldn't take this kind of medicine casually.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
忄 (heart) — 忄 is the heart radical for feelings, as in 情, 怕; 惜 is the feeling of cherishing.
昔 (xī) — same sound — 惜 is xī, like 昔 (in the past); 昔 also sounds out 借 jiè and 错 cuò.

example.hanzi: 他不惜一切代价去救那只受伤的小狗。
example.pinyin: tā bùxī yīqiè dàijià qù jiù nà zhī shòushāng de xiǎo gǒu.
example.english: He spared no cost to save the injured little dog.
example.fact: Wolves, the ancestors of domestic dogs, were first tamed by humans at least 15,000 years ago, making dogs the oldest domesticated animal — genetic evidence suggests some early dog lineages may even predate the rise of agriculture.

examples.hanzi: 为了赶上末班车，他不惜跑了两站路。
examples.pinyin: Wèile gǎn shàng mòbānchē, tā bùxī pǎo le liǎng zhàn lù.
examples.english: To catch the last bus, he didn't hesitate to run for two stops.

examples.hanzi: 她不惜花很多钱给孩子请好老师。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùxī huā hěn duō qián gěi háizi qǐng hǎo lǎoshī.
examples.english: She spares no expense to hire good teachers for her child.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.

example.hanzi: 老板因为报告迟交而对他发火了。
example.pinyin: lǎobǎn yīnwèi bàogào chí jiāo ér duì tā fāhuǒ le.
example.english: The boss got angry at him because the report was late.
example.fact: Anger triggers a surge of adrenaline and cortisol that raises heart rate and blood pressure within seconds; researchers have found that chronic anger and hostility are linked to a measurably higher risk of heart disease over a person's lifetime.

examples.hanzi: 别发火，我们慢慢说。
examples.pinyin: Bié fāhuǒ, wǒmen mànmàn shuō.
examples.english: Don't lose your temper, let's talk it through slowly.

examples.hanzi: 他很少发火，大家都觉得他脾气好。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn shǎo fāhuǒ, dàjiā dōu juéde tā píqi hǎo.
examples.english: He rarely gets angry, and everyone thinks he is good-tempered.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and prayer: 神, 福, 祈; 祷 is to pray aloud.
寿 (shòu) is only a loose sound clue; same part in 涛 tāo.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 说 say, 问 ask; 告 is "to tell". 告 also gives sound to 造 zào and 靠 kào.

example.hanzi: 每天晚上,奶奶都会安静地祷告。
example.pinyin: měitiān wǎnshàng, nǎinai dōu huì ānjìng de dǎogào.
example.english: Every night, grandma quietly prays.
example.fact: The oldest known written prayers come from ancient Sumer, inscribed in cuneiform on clay tablets more than 4,000 years ago, addressed to deities like Enlil and Inanna asking for protection, health, and good harvests.

examples.hanzi: 吃饭以前，他低头祷告了一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Chīfàn yǐqián, tā dītóu dǎogào le yíhuìr.
examples.english: Before eating, he bowed his head and prayed for a moment.

examples.hanzi: 大家一起为病人祷告，希望他早日康复。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā yìqǐ wèi bìngrén dǎogào, xīwàng tā zǎorì kāngfù.
examples.english: Everyone prayed for the patient, hoping for a quick recovery.

components.note: 月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: tasks take effort. The top 夂 stands in for the traditional 務.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 服务员,请给我们一壶热茶。
example.pinyin: fúwùyuán, qǐng gěi wǒmen yī hú rè chá.
example.english: Waiter, please bring us a pot of hot tea.
example.fact: Tipping is believed to have originated in 17th-century England, where wealthy patrons at coffeehouses would give small coins "to insure promptness" before their meal even arrived; the custom later spread to the United States after the Civil War.

examples.hanzi: 服务员，请把菜单拿给我们。
examples.pinyin: Fúwùyuán, qǐng bǎ càidān ná gěi wǒmen.
examples.english: Waiter, please bring us the menu.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店的服务员态度非常好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de fúwùyuán tàidù fēicháng hǎo.
examples.english: The staff at this hotel have a very good attitude.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 犭 is the animal radical, as in 猫, 狗, 狼; 犹 first named an animal.
尤 (yóu) — same sound — 犹 is yóu, like 尤; 尤 also sounds out 优 yōu.
予 (yǔ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 预 yù, as in 预备 to prepare.

example.hanzi: 面对两份工作机会,她犹豫了很久。
example.pinyin: miànduì liǎng fèn gōngzuò jīhuì, tā yóuyù le hěn jiǔ.
example.english: Facing two job offers, she hesitated for a long time.
example.fact: Buridan's ass is a philosophical paradox describing a hungry donkey placed exactly between two identical piles of hay, so perfectly balanced by reason that it cannot choose either and starves — used since the Middle Ages to illustrate the danger of excessive deliberation.

examples.hanzi: 你在犹豫什么？快做决定吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài yóuyù shénme? Kuài zuò juédìng ba.
examples.english: What are you hesitating about? Just make a decision.

examples.hanzi: 他毫不犹豫地跳进水里救人。
examples.pinyin: Tā háo bù yóuyù de tiào jìn shuǐ lǐ jiù rén.
examples.english: He jumped into the water to save someone without hesitation.

components.note: 水 (water) — water and flow: 永 first meant a long river. 泳 yǒng (swimming) added the water radical later.
忄 (heart) — a steady heart, hence constant; also in 快 happy, 慢 slow.
亘 (gèn) is only a loose sound clue for héng.

example.hanzi: 钻石常被用来象征永恒的爱情。
example.pinyin: zuànshí cháng bèi yòng lái xiàngzhēng yǒnghéng de àiqíng.
example.english: Diamonds are often used to symbolize eternal love.
example.fact: Diamonds form under intense heat and pressure roughly 150 to 200 kilometers below Earth's surface and are carried upward by volcanic eruptions; most of the diamonds mined today were forged more than a billion years ago, long before complex life existed on land.

examples.hanzi: 他们相信友谊是永恒的。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen xiāngxìn yǒuyì shì yǒnghéng de.
examples.english: They believe friendship is everlasting.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌表达了对永恒爱情的向往。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē biǎodá le duì yǒnghéng àiqíng de xiàngwǎng.
examples.english: This song expresses a longing for eternal love.

components.note: 人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".
此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".

example.hanzi: 他们相识之后,从此成了最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: tāmen xiāngshí zhīhòu, cóngcǐ chéngle zuì hǎo de péngyou.
example.english: After they met, they became best friends from then on.
example.fact: Charles Darwin and the botanist Joseph Hooker met in 1839 and remained close friends and scientific confidants for over 40 years; Hooker was one of the few people Darwin trusted with an early draft of his theory of evolution long before "On the Origin of Species" was published in 1859.

examples.hanzi: 从此，他再也没有迟到过。
examples.pinyin: Cóngcǐ, tā zài yě méiyǒu chídào guo.
examples.english: From then on, he was never late again.

examples.hanzi: 她搬到了北京，从此开始了新的生活。
examples.pinyin: Tā bān dào le Běijīng, cóngcǐ kāishǐ le xīn de shēnghuó.
examples.english: She moved to Beijing and started a new life from then on.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
亻 (person) — person radical (单人旁) — 价 is about what people pay or the worth of things; also in 你, 他, 住.
介 (jiè) — near-sound hint — 价 is jià; 介 also sounds out 界 jiè and 阶 jiē.

example.hanzi: 拍卖会上,他为那幅画出价十万元。
example.pinyin: pāimài huì shàng, tā wèi nà fú huà chūjià shí wàn yuán.
example.english: At the auction, he bid a hundred thousand yuan for that painting.
example.fact: In 2017, Leonardo da Vinci's painting "Salvator Mundi" sold at a Christie's auction for $450.3 million, making it the most expensive painting ever sold publicly — the final bid came after roughly 19 minutes of competing offers.

examples.hanzi: 有人愿意出价买这辆旧车吗？
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén yuànyì chūjià mǎi zhè liàng jiù chē ma?
examples.english: Is anyone willing to bid on this old car?

examples.hanzi: 他出价太低，卖家不同意。
examples.pinyin: Tā chūjià tài dī, màijiā bù tóngyì.
examples.english: His bid was too low, and the seller didn't agree.

meanings: to dismiss students at the end of the school day

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 孩子们放学后喜欢在操场上打篮球。
example.pinyin: háizimen fàngxué hòu xǐhuan zài cāochǎng shàng dǎ lánqiú.
example.english: After school lets out, the kids like to play basketball on the field.
example.fact: Basketball was invented in December 1891 by physical education instructor James Naismith in Springfield, Massachusetts, who nailed two peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony and wrote thirteen original rules to keep his students active during the cold New England winter.

examples.hanzi: 我每天下午四点放学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān xiàwǔ sì diǎn fàngxué.
examples.english: I get out of school at four every afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 放学以后，我们一起去买冰淇淋吧。
examples.pinyin: Fàngxué yǐhòu, wǒmen yìqǐ qù mǎi bīngqílín ba.
examples.english: After school, let's go buy ice cream together.

components.note: 礻 (spirit, from 示) — marks ritual and spirits, as in 神 god, 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; 祖 is an ancestor, honoured at the altar.
且 (qiě) hints at the sound: 祖 zǔ is close to 组 zǔ, 阻 zǔ and 租 zū.
父 (father) — a hand holding a stone axe, an image of the household head who works and rules.

example.hanzi: 我祖父年轻时是一名木匠。
example.pinyin: wǒ zǔfù niánqīng shí shì yī míng mùjiang.
example.english: My grandfather was a carpenter when he was young.
example.fact: The oldest confirmed woodworking joints, found at Israel's Jaljulia archaeological site, date back roughly 9,000 years, showing that carpentry techniques like mortise-and-tenon joinery are almost as old as settled agriculture itself.

examples.hanzi: 我祖父今年已经八十岁了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǔfù jīnnián yǐjīng bāshí suì le.
examples.english: My grandfather is already eighty this year.

examples.hanzi: 祖父每天早上都要打太极拳。
examples.pinyin: Zǔfù měi tiān zǎoshang dōu yào dǎ tàijíquán.
examples.english: My grandfather does tai chi every morning.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.hanzi: 时间不早了,我们回见吧。
example.pinyin: shíjiān bù zǎo le, wǒmen huíjiàn ba.
example.english: It's getting late, see you later then.
example.fact: The first mechanical clocks with escapements appeared in medieval European monasteries around the 13th century, built primarily to ring bells calling monks to prayer at consistent hours — a technology that eventually reshaped how all of society organized its day.

examples.hanzi: 我先走了，回见！
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiān zǒu le, huíjiàn!
examples.english: I'm off now, see you later!

examples.hanzi: 明天下午三点，我们回见。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān xiàwǔ sān diǎn, wǒmen huíjiàn.
examples.english: See you again tomorrow at three in the afternoon.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — marks bows and bending, as in 弯, 引, 张, 强; 弱 doubles the shape and pairs with 强 strong.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 每个超级英雄都有自己的弱点。
example.pinyin: měi gè chāojí yīngxióng dōu yǒu zìjǐ de ruòdiǎn.
example.english: Every superhero has their own weak point.
example.fact: In Greek mythology, the warrior Achilles was said to be invulnerable everywhere except his heel, the one spot his mother forgot to submerge in the river Styx — giving rise to the modern term "Achilles' heel" for a single critical vulnerability.

examples.hanzi: 懒惰是他最大的弱点。
examples.pinyin: Lǎnduò shì tā zuì dà de ruòdiǎn.
examples.english: Laziness is his biggest weakness.

examples.hanzi: 对手很快就发现了我们的弱点。
examples.pinyin: Duìshǒu hěn kuài jiù fāxiàn le wǒmen de ruòdiǎn.
examples.english: The opponent soon found our weak point.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.

example.hanzi: 愚人节那天,他跟同事开了一个恶作剧。
example.pinyin: yúrénjié nà tiān, tā gēn tóngshì kāile yī gè èzuòjù.
example.english: On April Fools' Day, he played a practical joke on his coworker.
example.fact: April Fools' Day's exact origin is debated, but one leading theory ties it to France's 1564 shift from the Julian calendar, which began the new year around April 1, to the Gregorian calendar starting January 1 — those who kept celebrating on the old date were mocked as "April fools."

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢搞恶作剧，大家都被他吓过。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan gǎo èzuòjù, dàjiā dōu bèi tā xià guo.
examples.english: He likes playing pranks, and everyone has been scared by him.

examples.hanzi: 这只是个恶作剧，别当真。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì ge èzuòjù, bié dàngzhēn.
examples.english: It's just a prank, don't take it seriously.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
车 (vehicle) — carrying loads by cart; also in 轮 wheel, 辆 for cars.
哉 (zāi) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 栽 zāi and 裁 cái. Note 载 reads zài in 下载.

example.hanzi: 请先下载这个应用程序再打开它。
example.pinyin: qǐng xiān xiàzǎi zhège yìngyòng chéngxù zài dǎkāi tā.
example.english: Please download this app first before opening it.
example.fact: The first file ever transferred over what became the internet was sent in 1969 between two computers at UCLA and Stanford Research Institute, roughly 500 kilometers apart; the system crashed after only the first two letters of "LOGIN" were successfully transmitted.

examples.hanzi: 我从网上下载了一首歌。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng wǎng shàng xiàzǎi le yì shǒu gē.
examples.english: I downloaded a song from the internet.

examples.hanzi: 下载速度太慢了，怎么办？
examples.pinyin: Xiàzǎi sùdù tài màn le, zěnme bàn?
examples.english: The download speed is too slow, what should I do?

components.note: 虫 (insect) — marks insects, as in 蜂 bee, 蚊 mosquito, 蜘 spider; 蜜 is what bees make: honey.
宓 (mì) gives the sound exactly: 蜜 mì, also in 密 mì.
月 — a crescent moon, also the word for month; in body words ⺼ is a different part, as in 脸 face.

example.hanzi: 他们打算去巴厘岛度蜜月。
example.pinyin: tāmen dǎsuàn qù bālí dǎo dù mìyuè.
example.english: They plan to spend their honeymoon in Bali.
example.fact: Bali's iconic terraced rice paddies rely on a centuries-old irrigation system called subak, a cooperative water-sharing network managed by farmer communities and temple priests that UNESCO recognized as a World Heritage Site in 2012 for embodying a philosophy of harmony between humans, nature, and the spiritual realm.

examples.hanzi: 我们的蜜月旅行去了海边。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de mìyuè lǚxíng qù le hǎibiān.
examples.english: We went to the seaside on our honeymoon.

examples.hanzi: 他们刚结婚，正在度蜜月。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen gāng jiéhūn, zhèngzài dù mìyuè.
examples.english: They just got married and are on their honeymoon.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 投 is to throw.
殳 (shū) is a weapon-in-hand part that is only a loose sound clue; it also appears in 设 shè and 段 duàn.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and language, as in 说 say, 请 please, 谢 thank.
斥 (chì) is only a loose sound hint for sù.

example.hanzi: 顾客向经理投诉了食物的质量问题。
example.pinyin: gùkè xiàng jīnglǐ tóusù le shíwù de zhìliàng wèntí.
example.english: The customer complained to the manager about the quality of the food.
example.fact: The world's oldest known consumer complaint is a nearly 3,750-year-old clay tablet from ancient Babylon, in which a customer named Nanni complained to a copper merchant named Ea-nasir that the copper delivered was of poor quality and the wrong grade.

examples.hanzi: 如果你不满意，可以向公司投诉。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ bù mǎnyì, kěyǐ xiàng gōngsī tóusù.
examples.english: If you're not satisfied, you can file a complaint with the company.

examples.hanzi: 邻居因为噪音投诉了我们。
examples.pinyin: Línjū yīnwèi zàoyīn tóusù le wǒmen.
examples.english: Our neighbor complained about us because of the noise.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — bird element as in 难, 谁, 集; in 雇 it is historical, so just treat it as a part.
户 (hù) — sounds out 雇 gù — close (same final, h→g); 户 also sounds out 顾 gù, so 雇 and 顾 sound alike.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 这家公司有超过五百名雇员。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu chāoguò wǔbǎi míng gùyuán.
example.english: This company has more than five hundred employees.
example.fact: The Ford Motor Company's decision in 1914 to pay assembly-line workers $5 a day — roughly double the prevailing wage — cut worker turnover dramatically and is often credited with helping create a stable American middle class able to afford the very cars it built.

examples.hanzi: 公司给雇员提供免费午餐。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī gěi gùyuán tígōng miǎnfèi wǔcān.
examples.english: The company offers its employees free lunch.

examples.hanzi: 这位雇员已经工作了十年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi gùyuán yǐjīng gōngzuò le shí nián.
examples.english: This employee has worked for ten years.

components.note: 月 — a crescent moon, also the word for month; in body words ⺼ is a different part, as in 脸 face.
亮 (liàng) is a sound clue for 谅 liàng and 晾 liàng; as a word it means bright, as in 月亮 moon.

example.hanzi: 今晚的月亮特别圆特别亮。
example.pinyin: jīnwǎn de yuèliang tèbié yuán tèbié liàng.
example.english: Tonight's moon is especially round and bright.
example.fact: The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at a rate of about 3.8 centimeters per year, a measurement possible because Apollo astronauts left retroreflectors on the lunar surface that scientists still bounce laser beams off today.

examples.hanzi: 月亮升起来了，星星也出来了。
examples.pinyin: Yuèliang shēng qǐlái le, xīngxing yě chūlái le.
examples.english: The moon has risen and the stars have come out too.

examples.hanzi: 中秋节的月亮最圆。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngqiūjié de yuèliang zuì yuán.
examples.english: The moon at Mid-Autumn Festival is the roundest.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
具 (tool) — two hands 廾 (the bottom 八) hold something valuable above — to provide, and a tool, as in 工具; 具 also sounds out 惧 jù.

example.hanzi: 新买的家具还没有送到我家。
example.pinyin: xīn mǎi de jiājù hái méiyǒu sòngdào wǒ jiā.
example.english: The furniture I just bought hasn't been delivered to my home yet.
example.fact: IKEA's flat-pack furniture concept began in 1956 when an employee named Gillis Lundgren removed the legs from a table so it would fit into his car, sparking the idea that shipping furniture unassembled could drastically cut transport costs and space.

examples.hanzi: 这张桌子是很好的家具。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì hěn hǎo de jiājù.
examples.english: This table is a fine piece of furniture.

examples.hanzi: 我们想买一些新家具。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiǎng mǎi yìxiē xīn jiājù.
examples.english: We would like to buy some new furniture.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a person 人 standing on tiptoe 止 to see farther; hence to aspire or plan (企图), also 企业 enterprise.
Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 这家企业去年的利润增长了三成。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā qǐyè qùnián de lìrùn zēngzhǎng le sān chéng.
example.english: This company's profits grew by thirty percent last year.
example.fact: The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, is considered the world's first publicly traded corporation; at its peak it issued its own currency, maintained a private army of roughly 10,000 soldiers, and its shares traded on what became the first formal stock exchange, in Amsterdam.

examples.hanzi: 他在一家大企业工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā dà qǐyè gōngzuò.
examples.english: He works at a large company.

examples.hanzi: 小企业需要政府的支持。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo qǐyè xūyào zhèngfǔ de zhīchí.
examples.english: Small businesses need the government's support.

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — cornered in a hole with no way out: exhausted, poor; also in 空 empty, 窗 window.

example.hanzi: 他小时候家里很穷。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎoshíhou jiālǐ hěn qióng.
example.english: His family was very poor when he was a child.
example.fact: 穷 is the plain word for poor, and 贫穷 is the formal version. Its older sense is "to exhaust," as in 无穷无尽 (endless) and 穷尽. People use it jokingly too: 我穷死了 means "I'm totally broke."

examples.hanzi: 他很穷，但是很快乐。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn qióng, dànshì hěn kuàilè.
examples.english: He is poor but very happy.

examples.hanzi: 那个穷孩子努力学习，后来考上了大学。
examples.pinyin: Nàge qióng háizi nǔlì xuéxí, hòulái kǎoshàng le dàxué.
examples.english: That poor child studied hard and later got into university.
